title: Incidence of colorectal polyps in repeat colonoscopies in patients after liver transplantation
summary:
Patients who have undergone a liver transplant face an increased risk of developing malignant tumors. It remains unclear whether this also applies to colorectal cancer. In particular, it is uncertain whether the risk is elevated in patients who do not suffer from a specific bile duct disorder or associated chronic inflammation of the colon.

Consequently, there are currently no general recommendations advising these patients to undergo colonoscopies more frequently than individuals who have not had a liver transplant.

Studies to date indicate that colon polyps—potential precursors to colorectal cancer—are found more frequently in patients following liver transplantation. These include polyps with a high risk of progressing to cancer. However, previous studies have only examined a single colonoscopy performed after the transplant.

Therefore, the impact of repeated colonoscopies on the detection rate of such polyps has not yet been sufficiently clarified. It is also unclear what significance a specific type of colon polyp holds regarding the development of colorectal cancer in liver transplant patients.

In the general population, it is estimated that up to one-third of colorectal cancer cases do not originate from conventional colon polyps. Instead, the cancer develops via an alternative pathway associated with a specific type of colon polyp.

At the Department of Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Transplantation Medicine, liver transplant patients are offered regular colonoscopies, typically performed every one to three years. This means these patients undergo examinations significantly more often than individuals without a liver transplant.

The planned research project aims to analyze data from a predefined group of patients who underwent liver transplantation at the University Hospital Essen. The study involves a retrospective analysis of existing medical data.

Patients who have previously had bowel cancer or who are known to have a hereditary condition that increases cancer risk are excluded from the study. Also excluded are patients with conditions associated with the formation of numerous bowel polyps, long-standing inflammatory bowel disease, or a specific chronic disease of the bile ducts.
conditions: Colorectal cancer screening in liver transplant recipients

interventions.name: Liver transplant patients undergoing recurrent colonoscopies for colorectal cancer screening as part of routine medical care, for the purpose of recording the incidence of colorectal neoplasms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Liver transplantation performed on or after January 1, 2007
•	Age ≥ 18 years at the time of transplantation
•	≥ 1 colonoscopy after liver transplantation
Exclusion criteria:
•	PSC prior to transplantation
•	Inflammatory bowel disease
•	Follow-up period < 12 months after liver transplantation
•	Colorectal carcinoma prior to transplantation
•	Colon carcinoma syndromes prior to transplantation, e.g., FAP, HNPCC (Lynch syndrome), etc.
